docs.title: Feature Highlights
docs.text:
• Multiple server profiles stored in RMS (persistent)
  • TLS-first with automatic plain fallback via gateway
  • Full RFC 2812 IRC protocol support
  • Per-channel ring buffers (200 lines scrollback)
  • Nick lists with modes (@ + % & ~ !)
  • Highlight badges + vibrate/beep on mention/PM
  • Tab nick completion in input field
  • 129 unit tests passing (protocol, core, session)
  • < 300 KB JAR after ProGuard optimization

docs.title: Running Chatterbox — Detailed Guide
docs.text: This guide covers building, testing, and running both the MIDlet (Java ME IRC client) and the Gateway Server (Python TLS relay).

docs.title: Required Tools
docs.text: Tool Version Install Command / Download JDK 8–21 sudo apt install openjdk-17-jdk (Ubuntu/Debian) Apache Ant 1.10+ sudo apt install ant Sun WTK 2.5.2 2.5.2 Oracle Archive or sudo apt install sun-java-wtk ProGuard 7.x+ SourceForge Python 3.11+ sudo apt install python3.11 python3.11-venv

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Set these in your shell profile (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc) or export before building:

# Required for preverify + emulator
export WTK_HOME=/opt/WTK2.5.2

# Optional but recommended for smaller JAR
export PROGUARD_HOME=/opt/proguard7.4

# Optional: for signing JAR (real device install)
export KEYSTORE=~/my.keystore
export KEY_ALIAS=myalias
export KEYSTORE_PASS=storepass
export KEY_PASS=keypass

Verify they're set: 

echo $WTK_HOME
echo $PROGUARD_HOME

docs.title: Full Release Build (Recommended)
docs.text:
cd /home/uday/chatterbox
ant dist

This runs: clean → compile → preverify → obfuscate → jar → jad

Output: - dist/chatterbox.jar — The MIDlet JAR (< 300 KB) - dist/chatterbox.jad — JAD descriptor for OTA install

docs.text:
# Clean all build artifacts
ant clean

# Compile only (no WTK needed)
ant compile

# Preverify classes (requires WTK_HOME)
ant preverify

# ProGuard shrink/optimize/obfuscate (requires PROGUARD_HOME)
ant obfuscate

# Package JAR only
ant jar

docs.title: Signing the JAR (for real devices)
docs.text:
# Requires KEYSTORE, KEY_ALIAS, KEYSTORE_PASS, KEY_PASS env vars
ant sign

Note: Nokia S60 requires a Trusted/Manufacturer certificate for ssl:// permission. Self-signed JARs will fail TLS on device. Use the gateway (see below) as a workaround.

docs.title: Running Unit Tests (Desktop)
docs.text:
Tests run on the desktop JDK — no WTK or ProGuard needed.

ant test

Expected output: 129 tests, all green (or similar count)

Test classes: - ProtocolParserTest — IRC line parsing, CTCP, numerics - CoreTest — Commands, string utils, session logic - SessionTest — Channel buffers, nick lists, highlights

docs.title: Running the Gateway Server
docs.text: The gateway accepts plain TCP from the MIDlet and establishes TLS to the real IRC server.

docs.title: Option 1: Docker (Quickest)
docs.text:
cd /home/uday/chatterbox/gateway

# Build image
docker build -t chatterbox-gateway .

# Run container
docker run -d \
  --name chatterbox-gw \
  -p 6667:6667 \
  -e GATEWAY_PASSWORD="your-shared-secret" \
  -e GATEWAY_IRC_HOST=irc.libera.chat \
  -e GATEWAY_IRC_PORT=6697 \
  chatterbox-gateway

Verify it's running: 

docker logs chatterbox-gw
# Should show: "Gateway listening on 0.0.0.0:6667"

docs.title: Option 2: Bare Metal (systemd)
docs.text:
cd /home/uday/chatterbox/gateway

# 1. Create service user
sudo useradd -r -s /bin/false gateway

# 2. Create install directory
sudo mkdir -p /opt/chatterbox-gateway
sudo cp server.py /opt/chatterbox-gateway/

# 3. Create venv and install deps
sudo python3 -m venv /opt/chatterbox-gateway/.venv
sudo /opt/chatterbox-gateway/.venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip

# 4. Install systemd service
sudo cp deploy/chatterbox-gateway.service /etc/systemd/system/
# Edit the service file to set GATEWAY_PASSWORD
sudo vim /etc/systemd/system/chatterbox-gateway.service

# 5. Start service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now chatterbox-gateway

# Check status
sudo systemctl status chatterbox-gateway
journalctl -u chatterbox-gateway -f

docs.title: Gateway Configuration (Environment Variables)
docs.text: Variable Default Required Description GATEWAY_PASSWORD — Yes Shared secret; client sends as first line GATEWAY_LISTEN_HOST 0.0.0.0 No Bind address GATEWAY_LISTEN_PORT 6667 No Plain TCP port for clients GATEWAY_IRC_HOST irc.libera.chat No Target IRC server GATEWAY_IRC_PORT 6697 No Target IRC port (TLS) GATEWAY_IRC_PASSWORD (empty) No PASS sent to IRC server GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT 10 No Messages/sec per connection GATEWAY_LOG_LEVEL INFO No DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR GATEWAY_TLS_VERIFY true No Set false for self-signed IRC certs

docs.title: Running on the Emulator (WTK)
docs.text:
# Requires WTK_HOME set
ant install-emu

This launches the WTK emulator and installs the JAD. In the emulator: 1. Open Chatterbox from the app list 2. Configure settings (see below) 3. Press Options → Connect

docs.title: Configuring the MIDlet (First Run)
docs.text:
On first launch, the app opens the Settings screen. Fill in:

Field Example Value Notes Server irc.libera.chat IRC network hostname Port 6697 TLS port (or 6667 for plain) Use TLS checked Tries ssl:// first Nick yournick Primary nickname Alt Nick yournick_ Fallback if taken Channels #channel1,#channel2 key Comma-separated; key optional Gateway Host your.server.ip If using gateway Gateway Port 6667 Gateway plain port Gateway Pass your-shared-secret Must match GATEWAY_PASSWORD

Press Options → Save, then Options → Connect.

docs.title: Connection Flow
docs.text:
┌─────────────┐     ssl://6697     ┌──────────────┐
│  MIDlet     │ ───────────────── │  IRC Server  │
│  (Phone)    │                    │  (TLS)       │
└─────────────┘                    └──────────────┘
       │
       │ (if TLS fails or disabled)
       ▼
┌─────────────┐     plain TCP      ┌──────────────┐     TLS      ┌──────────────┐
│  MIDlet     │ ───────────────── │   Gateway    │ ──────────  │  IRC Server  │
│  (Phone)    │  (sends password)  │  (your VPS)  │              │  (TLS)       │
└─────────────┘                    └──────────────┘              └──────────────┘

Key point: Enable Use TLS in settings. The MIDlet tries ssl://irc.host:6697 first. Only if that fails does it fall back to the gateway.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text: Principle Implementation Separation of concerns Protocol (proto) ≠ State (core) ≠ Network (net) ≠ UI (ui) ≠ Storage (rms) Testability Protocol & core have zero MIDP dependencies; run on desktop JDK Resource constraints Ring buffers, bounded queues, lazy loading, ProGuard optimization Robustness All I/O in try/catch, malformed input never crashes, graceful degradation Platform idioms LCDUI for forms, Canvas for chat (performance), RMS for persistence

docs.title: Message Flow (Inbound)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Network
    participant Connection
    participant ConnMgr as ConnectionManager
    participant Parser as ProtocolParser
    participant SessMgr as SessionManager
    participant Channel
    participant UI as ChatView

    Network->>Connection: read bytes
    Connection->>ConnMgr: onData(lines)
    ConnMgr->>Parser: parse(line)
    Parser-->>ConnMgr: IrcMessage
    ConnMgr->>SessMgr: handle(msg)
    SessMgr->>Channel: route to channel
    Channel->>Channel: add to ring buffer
    Channel->>Channel: check highlights
    SessMgr->>UI: callSerially(repaint)
    UI->>UI: paint(canvas)

docs.title: Message Flow (Outbound)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant UI as ChatView
    participant CmdProc as CommandProcessor
    participant SessMgr as SessionManager
    participant ConnMgr as ConnectionManager
    participant FQ as FloodQueue
    participant Connection
    participant Network

    User->>UI: type + send (* key)
    UI->>CmdProc: process(input)
    alt is command
        CmdProc->>CmdProc: parse /cmd
        CmdProc->>SessMgr: execute
    else is message
        CmdProc->>SessMgr: send PRIVMSG
    end
    SessMgr->>ConnMgr: send(line)
    ConnMgr->>FQ: enqueue(line)
    FQ->>FQ: rate limit (2/2s)
    FQ->>Connection: write(line)
    Connection->>Network: TCP/TLS write

docs.title: Message Flow (Inbound)
docs.text:
1. Network → Connection.run() reads bytes
  2. Connection → ConnectionManager.onData() receives lines
  3. ProtocolParser.parse() → IrcMessage objects
  4. SessionManager.handle() → Routes to Channel/Session
  5. Channel → Adds to ring buffer, checks highlights
  6. UI → ChatView.repaint() triggered via Display.callSerially()

docs.title: Message Flow (Outbound)
docs.text:
1. User input → ChatView.commandAction()
  2. CommandProcessor → Parses /cmd or treats as message
  3. SessionManager.send() → ConnectionManager.send()
  4. FloodQueue → Queues, rate-limits (2 msg/2s)
  5. Connection → Writes to socket

docs.title: proto/ — Protocol Layer (Pure Java)
docs.text:
Zero MIDP dependencies — runs on desktop JDK for unit tests.

Class Responsibility ProtocolParser Parses raw IRC lines → IrcMessage (RFC 2812 + CTCP) IrcMessage Immutable parsed message: prefix, command, params, tags Ctcp CTCP encoding/decoding (ACTION, VERSION, PING, etc.) CaseMapping RFC 1459 / RFC 2812 case mapping (ascii-only)

Key parsing features: - Handles malformed lines gracefully (never throws) - Supports message tags (@batch, @msgid — IRCv3) - CTCP extraction from PRIVMSG/NOTICE - Numeric command mapping (001, 353, 366, 433, etc.)

docs.title: core/ — Session State & Logic
net/ — Network Layer
docs.text:
Class Responsibility Connection Single socket lifecycle: connect, read loop, write queue ConnectionManager Multi-connection orchestration, reconnect logic SocketFactory Creates socket:// or ssl:// connections FloodQueue Token bucket: 2 messages per 2 seconds, burst 4 ConnectionConfig Immutable config: host, port, TLS, gateway, credentials

Reconnect State Machine:

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> DISCONNECTED
    DISCONNECTED --> CONNECTING: connect()
    CONNECTING --> CONNECTED: success
    CONNECTING --> BACKING_OFF: fail
    CONNECTED --> DISCONNECTED: disconnect/error
    BACKING_OFF --> CONNECTING: timer (backoff)
    BACKING_OFF --> DISCONNECTED: max retries exceeded

    note right of BACKING_OFF
        Exponential backoff:
        2s → 4s → 8s → 16s → 32s → 60s (capped)
    end note
  • Exponential backoff: 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s, 60s (capped)
  • Keepalive: PING every 90s, timeout 300s
  • Background/foreground handling via pauseApp()/startApp()

docs.title: rms/ — Persistent Storage (RecordStore)
ui/ — User Interface
docs.text:
Class Type Responsibility ChatterboxMIDlet MIDlet App lifecycle, Display access, global state ChatView Canvas Custom chat rendering, input handling, key events ChatCanvas Canvas Low-level drawing: text wrap, nick colors, selection SettingsScreen Form Profile configuration (all tabs) ServiceScreen List Server/channel list with badges HighlightScreen Form Highlight rule management IgnoreScreen Form Ignore list management QuickConnect Form One-shot connection dialog LogViewer Canvas Full-screen log browsing UrlHandler — URL detection, browser launch

ChatView Rendering Pipeline: 

paint(Graphics g)
  │
  ├─► calculateVisibleLines()     // Based on scrollOffset, font height
  ├─► for each visible line:
  │     ├─► parse: timestamp, nick, message
  │     ├─► measure: string widths, wrap if needed
  │     ├─► draw: background, timestamp, nick (color), message
  │     └─► highlight: yellow bg if highlighted
  └─► drawInputLine()             // Input field at bottom

Nick Colors: Deterministic hash of nick → 16-color palette (consistent across sessions).

docs.title: Threading Model
Memory Profile (Target: < 1 MB Heap)
docs.text:
Component Est. Heap Session + 10 channels × 200 lines ~200 KB Nick lists (50 nicks × 10 chans) ~50 KB RMS buffers (serialization) ~30 KB UI (fonts, images, canvas buffer) ~100 KB Protocol parser buffers ~10 KB Total ~400 KB

Optimizations: - String.intern() for repeated nicks/channels - Primitive arrays vs. Vector/ArrayList - Reuse StringBuilder for rendering - ProGuard: -optimize -obfuscate -shrink

docs.title: Performance Characteristics
docs.text: Operation Complexity Notes Message append O(1) Ring buffer Scroll render O(lines visible) ~10-15 lines Nick completion O(nicks in channel) Linear scan, < 1ms Highlight check O(rules × message len) Rules typically < 10 RMS save O(data size) < 5 KB, ~50ms Reconnect backoff O(1) TimerTask

docs.title: Security Boundaries
docs.text: Boundary Protection Network → Parser No allocation in hot path, bounded buffers Parser → Session Validated IrcMessage, no raw strings Session → UI callSerially() — no cross-thread UI access RMS → App Private record stores, no external access Gateway → IRC TLS 1.2+, cert verification (configurable)

on: [push, pull_request]

// test/src/com/chatterbox/test/ProtocolParserTest.java
public class ProtocolParserTest extends TestCase {

    public void testPrivmsgParsing() {
        String line = ":nick!user@host PRIVMSG #chan :Hello world";
        IrcMessage msg = ProtocolParser.parse(line);

        assertEquals("PRIVMSG", msg.getCommand());
        assertEquals("nick", msg.getPrefix().getNick());
        assertEquals("#chan", msg.getParams()[0]);
        assertEquals("Hello world", msg.getParams()[1]);
    }

    public void testCtcpAction() {
        String line = ":nick!u@h PRIVMSG #chan :" + (char)1 + "ACTION waves" + (char)1;
        IrcMessage msg = ProtocolParser.parse(line);

        assertTrue(msg.isCtcp());
        assertEquals("ACTION", msg.getCtcpCommand());
        assertEquals("waves", msg.getCtcpParams()[0]);
    }
}

docs.text: The Chatterbox gateway is a Python asyncio TLS relay that allows the MIDlet to connect via plain TCP while the gateway handles TLS to the IRC network. This avoids device-side certificate issues.

    participant Phone as  Phone
    participant GW as ️ Gateway
    participant IRC as  IRC Server

    Phone->>GW: TCP connect :6667
    GW-->>Phone: Connected
    Phone->>GW: PASS your-shared-secret
    alt Valid password
        GW->>IRC: TLS connect :6697
        IRC-->>GW: TLS handshake OK
        GW-->>Phone: :gateway NOTICE * :Gateway ready
        loop Relay Loop
            Phone->>GW: IRC protocol (NICK, USER, etc.)
            GW->>IRC: Forward bytes
            IRC->>GW: Server replies
            GW->>Phone: Forward bytes
        end
    else Invalid password
        GW-->>Phone: :gateway NOTICE * :Auth failed
        GW->>Phone: Close connection
    end

  --name chatterbox-gw \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 6667:6667 \
  -e GATEWAY_PASSWORD="your-shared-secret" \

docs.title: 1. Create User & Directory
docs.text:
sudo useradd -r -s /bin/false gateway
sudo mkdir -p /opt/chatterbox-gateway
sudo cp server.py /opt/chatterbox-gateway/
sudo chown -R gateway:gateway /opt/chatterbox-gateway

sudo /opt/chatterbox-gateway/.venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip

docs.text:
sudo tee /etc/chatterbox-gateway.env > /dev/null <<'EOF'
GATEWAY_PASSWORD=your-shared-secret
GATEWAY_IRC_HOST=irc.libera.chat
GATEWAY_IRC_PORT=6697
GATEWAY_LISTEN_HOST=0.0.0.0
GATEWAY_LISTEN_PORT=6667
GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT=10
GATEWAY_LOG_LEVEL=INFO
GATEWAY_TLS_VERIFY=true
EOF
sudo chown gateway:gateway /etc/chatterbox-gateway.env
sudo chmod 600 /etc/chatterbox-gateway.env

docs.text:
sudo cp deploy/chatterbox-gateway.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now chatterbox-gateway

docs.text:
sudo systemctl status chatterbox-gateway
sudo journalctl -u chatterbox-gateway -f

docs.title: ️ Configuration Reference
docs.text:
All config via environment variables:

Variable Required Default Description GATEWAY_PASSWORD Yes — Shared secret; client sends as first line GATEWAY_LISTEN_HOST No 0.0.0.0 Bind address (use 127.0.0.1 for local only) GATEWAY_LISTEN_PORT No 6667 Plain TCP port for clients GATEWAY_IRC_HOST No irc.libera.chat Target IRC server hostname GATEWAY_IRC_PORT No 6697 Target IRC port (usually 6697 TLS) GATEWAY_IRC_PASSWORD No (empty) PASS sent to IRC server (if needed) GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT No 10 Max messages/second per connection GATEWAY_LOG_LEVEL No INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR GATEWAY_TLS_VERIFY No true Set false for self-signed IRC certs GATEWAY_IDLE_TIMEOUT No 300 Seconds before closing idle connection

docs.text:
1. **Use TLS = ** (default): Tries ssl://irc.libera.chat:6697 first
  2. Success → Direct TLS, no gateway used
  3. Fail → Falls back to gateway
  4. **Use TLS = **: Always uses gateway
  5. **Gateway enabled + Use TLS = **: Forces gateway (useful for testing)

docs.title: Getting Started with Chatterbox
docs.text: This guide walks you through getting Chatterbox running on your Nokia phone in the shortest time possible.

docs.title: On Your Computer
docs.text:
• Java JDK 8–21 — for building
  • Apache Ant 1.10+ — build orchestration
  • Sun WTK 2.5.2 or Nokia S60 SDK — for preverify and emulator (required for device JAR)
  • ProGuard 7.x+ — optional but recommended for size optimization

docs.title: On Your Phone
docs.text:
• Nokia S60 3rd/5th Ed. or S40 3rd/5th Ed. with MIDP 2.0
  • ~500 KB free storage (for JAR + JAD + RMS)
  • Wi-Fi or 2G/3G data connection

docs.title: 1. Clone & Build
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/your-repo/chatterbox.git
cd chatterbox

# Set WTK path (adjust for your system)
export WTK_HOME=/opt/WTK2.5.2

# Build release JAR + JAD
ant dist

Output: dist/chatterbox.jar + dist/chatterbox.jad

docs.title: 2. Transfer to Phone (Choose One)
docs.text: Method Steps Bluetooth Pair phone PC → Send both files via OBEX → Open from Inbox Memory Card Copy to E:/Others/ or mass_memory/ → Open in File Manager OTA (Web) Host files on web server with correct MIME types → Open JAD URL in browser

docs.title: 3. First Run Configuration
docs.text:
On first launch, the Settings screen appears automatically. Fill in:

Server:       irc.libera.chat
Port:         6697
Use TLS:       (checked)
Nick:         yournick
Alt nick:     yournick_
Channels:     #channel1,#channel2
Real name:    Chatterbox User

Optional — Gateway (recommended for TLS issues): 

Gateway host: your.server.ip
Gateway port: 6667
Gateway pass: your-shared-secret

Press Options → Save, then Options → Connect.

docs.title: Connection Flow
docs.text:
┌─────────────┐     ssl://:6697     ┌──────────────┐
│  Chatterbox │ ──────────────────► │ irc.libera.chat │
│   (Phone)   │   (Direct TLS)      │   (IRC Network) │
└─────────────┘                     └──────────────┘
       │
       │ ssl:// fails (cert issue)
       ▼
┌─────────────┐     socket://:6667   ┌──────────────┐     TLS      ┌──────────────┐
│  Chatterbox │ ──────────────────► │   Gateway    │ ───────────► │ irc.libera.chat │
│   (Phone)   │   (Plain TCP)       │  (Your VPS)  │              │   (IRC Network) │
└─────────────┘                     └──────────────┘              └──────────────┘

The MIDlet tries direct TLS first. Only if that fails does it fall back to the gateway.

docs.title: Verify It Works
docs.text:
1. Connected — Status shows "Connected" + server welcome (001 numeric)
  2. Auto-joined — Channels from settings appear with nick lists
  3. Send a message — Press * (Star) or Green Call key to send
  4. Receive a message — Ask someone to ping you; badge appears on channel tab
  5. Nick completion — Type first letters of a nick + Tab to cycle

docs.title: 🆘 If Something Goes Wrong
docs.text:
Symptom Likely Cause Fix "Security error" on connect Device TLS cert blocked Use gateway (see above) "Connection refused" Wrong host/port or firewall Check server:port, try 6667 plain "Invalid JAD" MIME types wrong (OTA) Server must send text/vnd.sun.j2me.app-descriptor App won't install Self-signed on S60 Sign with dev cert or use gateway No channels joined Channels field empty Add comma-separated channels in Settings

See Troubleshooting for more.

Both files are required. The JAD tells the phone about the JAR (size, version, permissions).

docs.text: Nokia S60 requires Trusted/Manufacturer certificate for ssl:// (TLS) sockets. - Self-signed → "Security error" on ssl:// connect - Workaround: Use gateway (plain socket:// to gateway, gateway does TLS)

# 2. Get it signed (requires Symbian Signed account - no longer available)

docs.title: Security Notes
docs.text: Threat model, TLS handling, certificate management, and security considerations for Chatterbox.

docs.title: Assets to Protect
docs.text: Asset Sensitivity Threat IRC credentials (NickServ password) High Theft → account takeover Gateway password High Theft → gateway abuse Private messages Medium Eavesdropping Channel history Low Local device access Device identity Low Tracking

docs.title: Attack Vectors & Mitigations
docs.text: Vector Risk Mitigation MITM on phonegateway Medium Gateway password (shared secret), TLS to IRC MITM on gatewayIRC Low TLS 1.2+, cert verification (default) Malicious IRC server Low No client-side exec, input sanitized RMS data theft Low Phone lock code, no sensitive data in RMS Gateway compromise Medium Isolated VPS, minimal attack surface Phishing (fake gateway) Medium Verify gateway password, host key

docs.title: Direct TLS (Phone → IRC Server)
docs.text:
How it works: 1. MIDlet opens ssl://irc.libera.chat:6697 2. Phone JSSE validates server certificate against built-in root CAs 3. If valid → encrypted connection established 4. If invalid → "Security error", connection fails

Limitations on Nokia S60: - Root CA store: Fixed at manufacture (~2006-2010 vintage) - Missing modern CAs: Let's Encrypt, ISRG Root X1, etc. - Result: Most modern IRC networks fail direct TLS on device

Workarounds: 1. Gateway (recommended) — Phone uses plain TCP to your VPS, VPS does modern TLS 2. Developer certificate — Sign MIDlet with trusted cert (complex, see below) 3. Plain port — Connect to 6667 unencrypted (not recommended)

docs.title: Gateway TLS (Gateway → IRC Server)
docs.text:
How it works: 1. Gateway (Python ssl module) connects to irc.libera.chat:6697 2. Uses system CA store (updated via OS packages) 3. Validates hostname (SNI), certificate chain, expiration 4. GATEWAY_TLS_VERIFY=true (default) — enforces validation

Configuration: 

# Strict (default, recommended)
GATEWAY_TLS_VERIFY=true

# Permissive (self-signed IRC certs only)
GATEWAY_TLS_VERIFY=false

docs.title: Certificate Pinning (Advanced)
docs.text:
Not implemented. Could add: 

# In gateway server.py
context = ssl.create_default_context()
context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_REQUIRED
context.check_hostname = True
# Pin specific cert:
# context.load_verify_locations(cafile="libera-ca.pem")

docs.title: Shared Secret Model
docs.text:
Phone                          Gateway
  │                               │
  ├─ PASS <secret> ──────────────►│  Verify
  │                               │
  │◄── :gateway NOTICE * :OK ────┤
  │                               │
  ├─ NICK/USER ─────────────────►│  Relay to IRC
  │                               │

Security Properties: - Password sent in plaintext over phonegateway link - Mitigation: Gateway on VPS you control, phone on your network/VPN - Not a cryptographic auth — just access control

sudo ufw allow from 203.0.113.0/24 to any port 6667

GATEWAY_LISTEN_HOST=100.64.0.1  # Tailscale IP

context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_REQUIRED
context.load_verify_locations(cafile="client-ca.pem")

docs.title: What's Stored in RMS (RecordStore)
docs.text:
Store Contains Sensitivity chatterbox-profile-* Server, nick, gateway password, channels Medium chatterbox-settings UI prefs, highlights, ignore list Low chatterbox-log-* Chat history (last 1000 lines/channel) Low chatterbox-ignore Ignore masks Low

Note: NickServ/ChanServ passwords are NOT stored — sent only at connect via ServiceIdentify.

docs.title: Protecting Device Data
docs.text:
1. Phone lock code — Prevents physical access to RMS
  2. No sensitive data in logs — Passwords masked in /log
  3. Remote wipe — Uninstall app → RMS deleted

docs.title: Avoiding Credential Leaks
docs.text:
// GOOD: Password only in memory, sent once at connect
connection.send("PASS " + config.gatewayPassword);

// BAD: Never log passwords
System.out.println("PASS " + password);  // NEVER DO THIS

docs.title: Protocol Parser Hardening
docs.text:
// ProtocolParser.parse() - never throws, handles malformed
public static IrcMessage parse(String line) {
    // 1. Length limit (512 bytes per RFC)
    if (line.length() > 512) line = line.substring(0, 512);

    // 2. No control chars except CTCP delimiter

docs.text: Layer Check Phone → Gateway Plain TCP, shared secret auth, your VPS Gateway → IRC TLS 1.2+, cert verify, SNI, modern ciphers IRC Network Server-side: SASL, cloaking, TLS enforcement

docs.title: Recommended Gateway Hardening
docs.text:
# 1. Firewall - only necessary ports
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw allow 22/tcp      # SSH (your IP only)
sudo ufw allow 6667/tcp    # Gateway (your phone IP or VPN)
sudo ufw enable

# 2. Fail2Ban on gateway auth failures
# (See gateway.md for config)

# 3. Non-root user
sudo useradd -r -s /bin/false gateway
# Run as 'gateway' user (systemd does this)

# 4. Read-only filesystem (optional)
# systemd: ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/log

# 5. Resource limits
# systemd: LimitNOFILE=10000, LimitNPROC=50

docs.title: Why It's Needed
docs.text: Nokia S60 MIDP security model: - Untrusted domain (self-signed) → socket:// OK, ssl:// BLOCKED - Trusted domain (VeriSign/Thawte) → Both OK (certs expired/unavailable) - Manufacturer domain (Nokia signed) → Both OK (requires Nokia signing) - Developer domain (dev cert) → Both OK if cert installed on phone

docs.title: Creating a Developer Certificate
docs.text:
Requires: Nokia S60 SDK (Windows) or makecert/signtool from SDK.

# 1. Generate key pair + CSR
makecert -csr -o my.csr -k my.key -cn "Chatterbox Dev" -ou "Dev" -o "Me" -c "US"

# 2. Submit to Symbian Signed (service discontinued)
#    Alternative: Self-sign with OpenSSL, but phone won't trust it

# 3. If you have a dev cert (.cer):
#    - Install on phone: Bluetooth/email → Open → Install certificate
#    - Sign JAR:
signtool sign -keystore my.keystore -alias myalias \
  -storepass storepass -keypass keypass \
  dist/chatterbox.jar

docs.text:

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: Solutions to common issues with Chatterbox on device, emulator, gateway, and build.

docs.title: "Security Error" on Connect
docs.text:
Symptom: App shows "Security error" or "Permission denied" when connecting with TLS.

Cause: Nokia S60 requires a Trusted/Manufacturer certificate for ssl:// sockets. Self-signed certs are blocked.

Solutions: 1. Use the gateway (recommended) — Configure gateway in Settings, disable direct TLS 2. Developer certificate — Create with Nokia SDK makecert/signtool, install .cer on phone 3. Plain port — Connect to port 6667 without TLS (if network supports)

# Gateway setup (quickest fix)
# Server: your.vps.ip
# Port: 6667
# Gateway: enabled with password
# Use TLS: unchecked (or checked for auto-fallback)

docs.title: "Invalid JAD" / "JAR Size Mismatch"
docs.text:
Symptom: Install fails with "Invalid JAD" or "Jar size mismatch".

Cause: JAD file MIDlet-Jar-Size doesn't match actual JAR bytes.

Fix: 

ant clean dist  # Rebuilds both with correct size
# Verify:
ls -l dist/chatterbox.jar
grep MIDlet-Jar-Size dist/chatterbox.jad

docs.title: App Won't Install / "Corrupt JAR"
docs.text:
Symptom: "Application not valid", "Corrupt JAR", or install silently fails.

Causes & Fixes: | Cause | Fix | |-------|-----| | Transfer corrupted (Bluetooth) | Re-send, keep phone awake, don't interrupt | | JAD MIME type wrong (OTA) | Server must send text/vnd.sun.j2me.app-descriptor | | JAR > phone heap limit | Ensure < 300 KB (ProGuard), try debug build | | Wrong CLDC/MIDP version | Requires MIDP 2.0 / CLDC 1.1 | | Duplicate install | Uninstall first: Menu → Apps → Chatterbox → Options → Uninstall |

docs.title: Out of Memory / App Crashes
docs.text:
Symptom: "Out of memory", app closes unexpectedly, phone slows down.

Fixes: 1. Reduce scrollback: Settings → Scrollback lines → 100 (default 200) 2. Close other apps: Red key → close browser, maps, etc. 3. Restart phone: Clears heap fragmentation 4. Clear logs: /log clearall or Settings → Clear Logs

docs.title: Connection Drops Frequently
docs.text:
Symptom: Disconnects every few minutes, reconnects automatically.

Causes & Fixes: | Cause | Fix | |-------|-----| | NAT timeout (router) | Gateway GATEWAY_IDLE_TIMEOUT=120, phone keepalive 90s | | Phone sleep mode | Disable "Power saver" or keep app in foreground | | 2G/3G signal loss | Enable Reconnect (default), increase backoff cap | | Server ping timeout | Increase keepalive: Settings → Keepalive → 120 |

docs.title: Vibrate/Beep Not Working
docs.text:
Symptom: No vibration or sound on highlight/PM.

Fixes: 1. Profile check: Not in Silent/Meeting/Offline profile 2. Settings: Settings → Vibrate on highlight → 3. Device support: S40 devices lack vibrate API (silent only) 4. Volume: Media volume up (not ringtone)

docs.title: Non-Latin Characters Broken
docs.text:
Symptom: Cyrillic/Greek/CJK shows as boxes or garbage.

Fixes: 1. Font support: Device must have font for script 2. Encoding: Server must send UTF-8 (modern networks do) 3. Workaround: /set encoding utf-8 (if supported)

docs.title: WTK Emulator Won't Start
docs.text:
Symptom: emulator command not found or fails.

Fixes: 

# Check WTK_HOME
echo $WTK_HOME
# Should be: /opt/WTK2.5.2

# Check binary
ls $WTK_HOME/bin/emulator

# Run directly
$WTK_HOME/bin/emulator

docs.title: "Preverify Failed" / Class Format Error
docs.text:
Symptom: Build fails at preverify step.

Causes: | Cause | Fix | |-------|-----| | JDK too new (class file version) | Use -source 1.5 -target 1.5 (build.xml does this) | | WTK version mismatch | Must be WTK 2.5.2 exactly | | ProGuard ran before preverify | Order: compile → preverify → proguard |

docs.title: Network Not Working in Emulator
docs.text:
Symptom: Can't connect to IRC/gateway from emulator.

Fixes: 1. WTK: Uses host network directly — check firewall 2. S60 SDK: Set networking to "Ethernet" or "Loopback" in SDK preferences 3. Gateway: Test with telnet localhost 6667 from host

docs.title: RMS Not Persisting in Emulator
docs.text:
Symptom: Settings lost on emulator restart.

Fix: WTK stores RMS in $WTK_HOME/appdb/ — don't delete this folder. Use ant install-emu not manual JAD install.

docs.title: Gateway Won't Start
docs.text:
Symptom: systemctl status chatterbox-gateway shows failed.

Debug: 

# Check logs
sudo journalctl -u chatterbox-gateway -n 50

# Common errors:
# - Address already in use → change GATEWAY_LISTEN_PORT
# - Permission denied → port < 1024 needs root (use 6667)
# - Config missing → check /etc/chatterbox-gateway.env

docs.title: Client Connects But No Relay
docs.text:
Symptom: Phone connects to gateway, but no IRC traffic flows.

Debug: 

# Check gateway logs
sudo journalctl -u chatterbox-gateway -f

# Should see:
# Client connected: <phone-ip>
# TLS established to irc.libera.chat:6697
# Relay started

# If missing "TLS established":
# - Check GATEWAY_IRC_HOST/PORT reachable from VPS
# - Test: openssl s_client -connect irc.libera.chat:6697

docs.title: "Authentication Failed" in Gateway Logs
docs.text:
Symptom: Gateway logs "Authentication failed from ".

Cause: Phone gateway password ≠ GATEWAY_PASSWORD.

Fix: 

# Verify match
# Phone Settings → Gateway pass: "mysecret"
# Server /etc/chatterbox-gateway.env: GATEWAY_PASSWORD=mysecret

docs.title: Rate Limiting Too Aggressive
docs.text:
Symptom: Messages dropped during busy conversation.

Fix: 

# Increase limit
GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT=20
# Or disable (not recommended for public)
GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT=0

# Restart
sudo systemctl restart chatterbox-gateway

docs.title: TLS Verification Fails
docs.text:
Symptom: Gateway logs TLS handshake error to IRC server.

Fix: 

# For self-signed IRC certs (rare)
GATEWAY_TLS_VERIFY=false

# Normal: leave true (default)
GATEWAY_TLS_VERIFY=true

docs.title: WTK_HOME Not Set
docs.text:
Error: WTK_HOME not set or preverify not found

Fix: 

export WTK_HOME=/opt/WTK2.5.2
# Add to ~/.bashrc for persistence
echo 'export WTK_HOME=/opt/WTK2.5.2' >> ~/.bashrc

docs.title: ProGuard Not Found / JAR Too Large
docs.text:
Symptom: dist/chatterbox.jar > 500 KB, ProGuard step skipped.

Fix: 

export PROGUARD_HOME=/opt/proguard7.4
# Verify
ls $PROGUARD_HOME/lib/proguard.jar

# Check build output for "proguard" task
ant dist 2>&1 | grep -i proguard

docs.title: "Cannot Find Symbol" for MIDP Classes
docs.text:
Error: Compilation fails on javax.microedition.* classes.

Cause: WTK libs not in classpath.

Fix: 

# Check build.xml has correct paths
grep midpapi build.xml
# Should reference ${wtk.lib}/midpapi20.jar

# Verify WTK_HOME/lib contents
ls $WTK_HOME/lib/
# midpapi20.jar, cldcapi11.jar must exist

docs.title: Signing Fails
docs.text:
Error: ant sign fails with keystore errors.

Fix: 

# All 4 env vars required
export KEYSTORE=/path/to/keystore
export KEY_ALIAS=myalias
export KEYSTORE_PASS=storepass
export KEY_PASS=keypass

# Verify keystore
keytool -list -keystore $KEYSTORE -storepass $KEYSTORE_PASS
